title: Add registry-cache Application (docker.io, per-DC)
body:
## Summary
Fourth and final per-cache migration to ArgoCD. Pull-through cache for `registry-1.docker.io` — the highest-traffic of the three registry caches, used by containerd on every k3s node.

Per-DC layout (vrtx/ldc/azpl) + alias vrtx Service + NodePort metrics (`30501` vrtx, `30511` ldc) — same shape as `registry-cache-mcr` and `registry-cache-gcr`.

**One notable difference**: docker.io Services expose only ports `5000` (registry) and `5001` (metrics), with no `443`/`80` aliases. Containerd consumes this as a registry mirror (`mirrors.docker.io.endpoint`), not as an HTTPS upstream — port aliases were unused in the legacy manifests and would only add adoption diff.

Pods already running from `roles/arc_setup`. ArgoCD adopts.

## Follow-up
After this lands, one bulk PR to `ans_playbooks` removing `roles/arc_setup/tasks/registry_cache_topology.yml` (or trimming to just the `zone-labeler` DaemonSet, which stays).

title: feat(arc-runner): apt-cache per-zone /etc/hosts (zastępuje watchdog + CoreDNS rewrite)

## Summary

- Dodaje per-zone apt-cache `/etc/hosts` override do `configure-registry-mirrors` init-containera w obu runner setach (`arc-runner-set`, `arc-runner-set-org`)
- Ten sam wzorzec co registry-cache w dind: sprawdź gotowość przez endpoints, zapisz ClusterIP do `/etc/hosts` jeśli ready, pomiń jeśli nie → fallback do internetu

- Per-zone: AZPL eviction nie dotyka LDC/VRTX
- Built-in fallback: brak ready endpoints = brak override = apt idzie do internetu bezpośrednio

title: fix(arc): remove oci:// prefix from repoURL for ArgoCD v3 compatibility
body:
## Summary

- Remove `oci://` prefix from `repoURL` in `arc`, `arc-runner-set`, and `arc-runner-set-org` Applications
- ArgoCD v3.x changed OCI Helm chart URL handling — the `oci://` prefix in `repoURL` caused the revision resolution step to query the registry without the chart name, resulting in 403 from ghcr.io
- With the prefix removed, ArgoCD uses `enableOCI: true` from the repo secret to detect OCI, and correctly builds the full path including the chart name

## Context

Upgraded ArgoCD v2.14.11 (chart 7.9.1) → v3.4.2 (chart 9.5.14). In v3.x, a new OCI digest resolution step was added that queries the registry v2 API. When `repoURL` contains `oci://`, this step strips the prefix but doesn't append the chart name, causing:

```
failed to resolve revision "0.14.0": cannot get digest for revision 0.14.0:
HEAD "https://ghcr.io/v2/actions/actions-runner-controller-charts/manifests/0.14.0"
```

The correct URL should include the chart name:
```
https://ghcr.io/v2/actions/actions-runner-controller-charts/gha-runner-scale-set-controller/manifests/0.14.0
```

The `arc-helm-oci-repo` k8s secret URL was also patched from `oci://ghcr.io/...` to `ghcr.io/...`.

## Test plan

- [ ] ArgoCD `arc` app shows `Synced + Healthy`
- [ ] ArgoCD `arc-runner-set` app shows `Synced + Healthy`
- [ ] ArgoCD `arc-runner-set-org` app shows `Synced + Healthy`

title: feat(apt-cache): CoreDNS rewrite + PreferClose dla per-zone APT cache
body:
## Summary

- **CoreDNS rewrite** (`coredns.yaml`): statyczny ConfigMap `coredns-custom` z 9 rewrite rules dla hostów apt. Zastępuje dynamiczny watchdog — `apt-cache` pody mają `dnsPolicy: None` + `1.1.1.1`, więc nie ma pętli DNS.
- **`trafficDistribution: PreferClose`** (`apt-cache.yaml`): kube-proxy preferuje endpoint w tej samej strefie co klient (na podstawie `topology.kubernetes.io/zone` ustawianego przez zone-labeler DaemonSet).

## Dlaczego

APT cache (`apt-cache-vrtx/ldc/azpl`) działał od 2026-05-14 ale żaden runner nie używał go — `coredns-custom` miał pusty `apt-cache.override`. Ruch z netbox-wg `docker build` i runner `apt-get` szedł prosto do internetu.

## Jak działa

```
docker build RUN apt-get / runner apt-get
  → 127.0.0.11 (Docker DNS) → upstream: CoreDNS
  → rewrite: ubuntu.task.gda.pl → apt-cache.arc-runners.svc.cluster.local
  → PreferClose: kube-proxy wybiera apt-cache-ldc dla LDC runnera
  → apt-cache-ldc → 1.1.1.1 → ubuntu.task.gda.pl (real mirror)
  → cache HIT przy kolejnych requestach
```

## Test plan

- [ ] ArgoCD sync `apt-cache` app — Synced + Healthy
- [ ] `kubectl get configmap coredns-custom -n kube-system -o jsonpath='{.data.apt-cache\.override}'` — nie pusty

title: feat(apt-cache): watchdog toggleuje CoreDNS rewrite per-zone health
body:
## Problem

PR #11 (zamknięty) dodawał `trafficDistribution: PreferClose` bez watchdoga.
PreferClose to *soft preference* — gdy lokalna strefa straci endpoint, kube-proxy
**fallbackuje do innej strefy przez Tailscale VPN**. To gorsze niż bezpośredni internet.

## Rozwiązanie

Watchdog Deployment monitoruje EndpointSlice per-zone i toggleuje `coredns-custom`
ConfigMap w `kube-system`:

| Stan | apt-cache.override | Routing |
|------|--------------------|---------|
| Wszystkie strefy zdrowe | 9 rewrite rules aktywnych | PreferClose → local zone cache ✓ |
| Jakakolwiek strefa pada (≥2 check) | `""` (disabled) | apt resolves do prawdziwych IPs → direct internet ✓ |

**Gwarancja: żadnego cross-zone ruchu przez Tailscale VPN w żadnym stanie.**

## Szczegóły implementacji

- `watchdog.yaml`: ServiceAccount + Role (endpointslice w arc-runners) + ClusterRole (configmap coredns-custom w kube-system) + Deployment
- `apt-cache.yaml`: dodano `trafficDistribution: PreferClose` na generic Service
- `coredns-custom` ConfigMap **nie jest zarządzany przez ArgoCD** (nie w manifests/) → selfHeal nie cofa zmian watchdoga
- Watchdog sprawdza EndpointSlice lokalnie (API call w klastrze, zero ruchu cross-VPN)
- Debounce 2×15s = 30s przed wyłączeniem rewrite — eliminuje flapping przy krótkich restartach podów

## Trade-off

AZPL Spot eviction → watchdog wyłącza rewrite → VRTX/LDC tracą cachowanie na ~60-120s (czas aż nowy node wstanie i apt-cache-azpl pod będzie ready). W tym czasie VRTX/LDC idą bezpośrednio do internetu — suboptymalne ale poprawne (żadnych cross-VPN).

## Test plan

- [ ] ArgoCD sync → watchdog pod Running
- [ ] `kubectl logs -n arc-runners deploy/apt-cache-watchdog` — widać "all zones healthy → enabling CoreDNS rewrite"
- [ ] `kubectl get configmap coredns-custom -n kube-system -o jsonpath='{.data.apt-cache\.override}'` — widać 9 rewrite rules
- [ ] Ręcznie scale down `apt-cache-azpl` do 0 replik → po ~30s watchdog loguje "unhealthy" i czyści ConfigMap
- [ ] `nslookup archive.ubuntu.com` z runner poda → powinno zwrócić prawdziwy IP (nie ClusterIP apt-cache)
- [ ] Scale up z powrotem → po ~15s rewrite wraca

title: feat(arc): add arc-runner-set-org-fast scale set
body:
## Summary

- Nowa scale set `arc-runner-set-org-fast` dla lekkich jobów org (bash/curl/jq, bez Dockera)
- Brak dind — runner odpala się bez sidecara docker daemon
- Zasoby: 500m CPU / 256Mi RAM vs 3 CPU / 4Gi dla pełnego runnera (~8× mniejszy)
- min=2 (zawsze ciepłe, zero cold-start), max=10
- Label: `builder-org-fast` — workflow używa `runs-on: [self-hosted, builder-org-fast]`
- `terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 60` (vs 600 — krótkie joby nie potrzebują długiego grace)

Zmienić w `Majowka/ans_playbooks` workflow `Auto-deploy on role/compose change`:
```yaml
runs-on: [self-hosted, builder-org-fast]
```
zamiast `[self-hosted, builder-org]`

- [ ] ArgoCD wykrywa nową Application i syncuje

title: fix(zproxy-k3s): ProxyBufferMode=memory żeby ukrócić korupcję sqlite
body:
## Problem

`zproxy-k3s` wpadł w CrashLoopBackOff (104 restarty / 8h):

```
[Z3005] query failed: [0] database disk image is malformed [pragma synchronous=0]
database is down: reconnecting in 10 seconds
```

Baza SQLite na `emptyDir` się uszkodziła. Pętla nie przerywa się sama:
- `emptyDir` przeżywa restart kontenera (cykl życia = pod, nie kontener) → malformed DB zostaje
- `init-container` biega tylko przy tworzeniu poda, nie przy restarcie kontenera
- ArgoCD self-heal naprawia dryf configu, nie korupcję w runtime
- jedyny ratunek doraźny to `kubectl delete pod` (zrobione — pod wstał czysty)

## Przyczyna

W trybie `disk` (default) **każda zebrana wartość** przechodzi przez SQLite. Ten ciągły ruch zapisu + twardy SIGKILL (liveness probe / OOM) w trakcie transakcji = malformed image. Przy `pragma synchronous=0` (brak fsync, trade-off za wydajność bufora) okno korupcji jest spore.

## Rozwiązanie

`ProxyBufferMode=memory` — funkcja wprowadzona w Zabbix 7.0. Zebrana historia/discovery/autoregistration buforowana jest **w RAM**, nie w bazie. SQLite zostaje tylko nośnikiem danych konfiguracyjnych synchronizowanych z serwera → rzadkie zapisy → write pressure na pliku spada praktycznie do zera.

`memory` (nie `hybrid`) jest właściwy dla tego proxy: bufor i tak siedzi na ulotnym `emptyDir`, więc „dane porzucone przy restarcie" to dla nas nie-problem. `hybrid` flushowałby do tego samego ulotnego SQLite — mniejszy zysk.

## Zmiany

- `ZBX_PROXYBUFFERMODE=memory`
- `ZBX_PROXYMEMORYBUFFERSIZE=96M` (wymagane != 0, inaczej proxy nie startuje)
- memory request `256Mi → 320Mi` — pokrycie na +96M segmentu shared-mem bufora

## Test plan

- [ ] ArgoCD syncuje `apps/zproxy-k3s` → `Synced + Healthy`
- [ ] `kubectl -n monitoring logs deploy/zproxy-k3s` — brak `database disk image is malformed`, proxy startuje i łączy się z serwerem
- [ ] proxy `zproxy-k3s.k3s.majowka.me` online w Zabbix UI, itemy z in-cluster Services aktualne
- [ ] pod stabilny — 0 restartów po kilku godzinach

Powiązany PR (rejestracja w Zabbixie): [ans_playbooks#62](https://github.com/Majowka/ans_playbooks/pull/62).

## Dlaczego StatefulSet, nie `replicas: 3` Deploymentu

Każdy Zabbix proxy to **osobny, nazwany byt** — własna nazwa, własna baza, własna rejestracja server-side. Trzy identyczne repliki Deploymentu zalogowałyby się jako ten sam proxy → konflikt. HA = Proxy Group, w której serwer rozdziela monitorowane hosty między żywych członków i przepina je przy awarii.

title: Bypass cluster DNS where it bites: ndots:2 for zproxy-k3s + external DNS for ARC listeners
body:
## Summary

Two fixes for the same underlying bug: glibc NSS aborts the resolution chain when a kubelet-injected search domain returns SERVFAIL. Reproduced today on `zproxy-k3s-0` (worker13/AZPL) hitting Service-DNS for monitoring probes — Zabbix HTTP_AGENT failed with `Could not connect to server` even though `nslookup` returned the right ClusterIP.

Root cause walkthrough (verified, not theorized):

| Test from `zproxy-k3s-0` | Result |
|---|---|
| `nslookup registry-cache-gcr-azpl.arc-runners.svc.cluster.local` | OK 10.43.120.120 |
| `getent hosts ...local` (no trailing dot) | empty |
| `getent hosts ...local.` (absolute) | OK 10.43.120.120 |
| `wget http://...local./metrics` | 200 OK + metrics |
| `wget http://...local/metrics` (no dot) | "bad address" |

`nslookup` bypasses NSS. `getent`/libcurl go through NSS, which with `ndots:5` (k8s default) expands every search domain before trying the absolute name. One of the kubelet's search entries — `tail07246.ts.net` (injected by Tailscale with `accept-dns=true` on workers) — returns SERVFAIL upstream, which makes glibc give up the chain.

## Changes

- **`apps/zproxy-k3s/manifests/zproxy-k3s.yaml`** — add `dnsConfig.options ndots: "2"` to StatefulSet. 4-dot FQDNs skip search expansion; short k8s names (`kubernetes`, `foo.default`) still resolve via search.
- **`apps/arc-runner-set*/values.yaml`** — codify `listenerTemplate` with `dnsPolicy: None` + `8.8.8.8/8.8.4.4` for all three scale-sets. The `k3s-arc` listener already had this applied via `kubectl edit` (drift not reflected in source — survived only thanks to `ServerSideApply=true`). The two org scale-sets were on default `ClusterFirst` and were one CoreDNS hiccup away from a stuck listener. Listeners only need GitHub API + k8s API (via env-var ClusterIP) — cluster DNS is pure liability for them.

## Why not "fix it at source" (Tailscale)

Long-term yes — `accept-dns=false` on workers (master nodes already have it) would remove the search-domain entirely. That's a rolling change on every worker with cordon/drain semantics — separate PR. This one stops the bleeding without touching the data plane.

## Test plan

- [ ] ArgoCD syncs `zproxy-k3s` Application -> StatefulSet rolls 2 pods. Verify `kubectl exec zproxy-k3s-0 -- cat /etc/resolv.conf` shows `options ndots:2`.
- [ ] Zabbix trigger `Registry cache pod unreachable on registry-cache (GCR) AZPL` returns to OK within 5 min.
- [ ] `kubectl get autoscalingrunnerset -n arc-runners -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}: {.spec.listenerTemplate.spec.dnsPolicy}{\"\n\"}{end}'` shows `None` for all 3.
- [ ] Pre-existing `k3s-arc` listener does not flap.
- [ ] `k3s-arc-org` and `k3s-arc-org-fast` listeners are re-created with `dnsPolicy: None` and continue processing jobs.

* **Chores**

  * Tuned proxy DNS resolver behavior to reduce search-domain expansion and stabilize hostname resolution within cluster workloads.

title: chore: revert DNS bypass workarounds — accept-dns=false rollout completed
body:
## Summary

ans_playbooks#81 (Semaphore task 158, 2026-05-26 16:57Z) rolled out \`tailscale set --accept-dns=false\` to all 14 k3s workers, removing \`*.tail07246.ts.net\` from their resolv.conf search domains. That eliminates the glibc NSS SERVFAIL search trap at the node level, so the pod-side workarounds from #27 are no longer needed.

## Changes

- \`apps/zproxy-k3s/manifests/zproxy-k3s.yaml\` — drop \`dnsConfig.options ndots:1\` (back to k8s default ndots:5)
- \`apps/arc-runner-set*/values.yaml\` (×3) — drop \`listenerTemplate.spec.{dnsConfig, dnsPolicy: None}\`, keep only \`containers: [{name: listener}]\` (CRD-required) + \`nodeSelector: {internet-access: true}\`

## Why revert (per architecture principle)

CoreDNS is now the single DNS egress for all in-cluster pods. The **only intentional bypasses** are the registry-cache* and apt-cache pods themselves — they MUST hit real upstream registries/mirrors directly because workers' \`/etc/hosts\` maps those public names (\`mirror.gcr.io\`, \`registry-1.docker.io\`, \`archive.ubuntu.com\` …) back to the cache ClusterIPs. A cache pod going through cluster DNS would resolve itself and loop.

Single rule: bypass CoreDNS only if you ARE the cache that would otherwise loop.

title: refactor(zproxy-k3s): StatefulSet → 2× Deployment for self-healing on node loss
body:
## Summary

Replace the `zproxy-k3s` StatefulSet with two Deployments (one per logical proxy identity) so the pods can self-heal when a worker node becomes Unreachable.

## Why

Production today (2026-05-28) demonstrated the StatefulSet sticky-identity trap:

- `zproxy-k3s-0` got stuck in `Terminating` state for ~16h after `k3s-worker9` went Unreachable (Azure Spot eviction)
- K3S-ProxyGroup dropped to 1/2 (pavailable=50%) and stayed there until manual intervention
- StatefulSet refuses to create a replacement with the same ordinal until the old pod is fully gone, and the old pod can never finish terminating because the dead kubelet on the unreachable node never acknowledges the deletion

Deployments don't share that constraint. With `tolerationSeconds: 30` (vs the K8s default 300s), the ReplicaSet schedules a replacement on a healthy node within ~1 minute. No stuck-Terminating wait, no operator paged at 3 AM.

## What changed

| | Before (StatefulSet) | After (2× Deployment) |
|---|---|---|
| Pod identity source | `metadata.name` via downward API (sticky to ordinal) | hardcoded `ZBX_HOSTNAME` env per Deployment |
| Self-heal on node Unreachable | ❌ stuck Terminating until old pod cleaned up | ✅ ~1min (30s `tolerationSeconds` + ReplicaSet) |
| Self-heal on node reboot/crash | ❌ waits for original node | ✅ ReplicaSet places replacement anywhere |
| podAntiAffinity (rozproszenie 2 nodes) | ✅ | ✅ (shared `app: zproxy-k3s` label) |
| PodDisruptionBudget minAvailable=1 | ✅ | ✅ |
| Update strategy | RollingUpdate (default) | `Recreate` (avoids double-`ZBX_HOSTNAME` rejection) |
| Per-pod stable DNS | headless Service `zproxy-k3s-N.zproxy-k3s...` | ClusterIP per-instance `zproxy-k3s-{0,1}.monitoring...` |
| emptyDir per replica | ✅ | ✅ |

`ProxyBufferMode=memory` makes this safe: the sqlite DB only holds server-synced config (refreshed on startup), so there's no persistent state worth preserving across pod replacement.

## Migration after merge

ArgoCD will:
1. Apply the new Deployments + per-instance Services (`zproxy-k3s-0`, `zproxy-k3s-1`)
2. Prune the old StatefulSet `zproxy-k3s` + headless Service `zproxy-k3s` (per `syncPolicy.automated.prune=true`)

One-time manual step after sync:
\`\`\`bash
# Remove the already-stuck-Terminating pod that StatefulSet deletion left orphaned
kubectl delete pod zproxy-k3s-0 -n monitoring --force --grace-period=0
\`\`\`

## Test plan

- [x] YAML validates (\`python3 -c "yaml.safe_load_all"\`): 5 docs (2× Service, 2× Deployment, 1× PDB)
- [ ] ArgoCD picks up the change and applies cleanly
- [ ] Both new pods (\`zproxy-k3s-0-*\`, \`zproxy-k3s-1-*\`) reach Ready within ~2min
- [ ] K3S-ProxyGroup \`pavailable\` returns to 100 (verify in Zabbix \`zabbix.majowka.me\`: \`last(/Zabbix server health/zabbix.proxy.group.avail.proxies.percent[K3S-ProxyGroup])\`)
- [ ] Functional check: in-cluster monitored services (apt-cache, registry-cache) keep reporting via proxy group
- [ ] **Self-heal validation**: simulate node Unreachable via \`kubectl cordon\` + \`kubectl delete pod --force\` on one pod's node — replacement should appear on the surviving node within ~1min

title: fix(zproxy-k3s): init-data runs as non-root, drop chown/chmod (PROD INCIDENT)
body:
## Production incident

Both `zproxy-k3s-0` and `zproxy-k3s-1` Deployments are 0/1 with pods in `Init:CrashLoopBackOff` for ~4.5h. K3S-ProxyGroup is offline:

\`\`\`
zabbix.proxy.group.state[K3S-ProxyGroup]              = 1   (offline)
zabbix.proxy.group.avail.proxies.percent[K3S-ProxyGroup] = 0
zabbix.proxy.group.avail.proxies[K3S-ProxyGroup]      = 0
\`\`\`

In-cluster monitoring via this proxy group (apt-cache, registry-cache, etc.) is degraded.

## Root cause

The original PR #59 included this fix on the branch (commit e384c29) but the squash-merge picked an earlier snapshot from the branch that still contained the legacy root + chown init step.

Then the b66d3e6 security hardening (also in #59) dropped all capabilities on the init container — including `CAP_CHOWN`. The container still ran as uid 0, but `chown -R 1997:1995 /var/lib/zabbix` failed with "Operation not permitted" because no capability allows chown without `CAP_CHOWN`. Pods loop on init-data failure indefinitely.

\`\`\`
$ kubectl logs -n monitoring zproxy-k3s-0-... -c init-data
chown: /var/lib/zabbix/db_data: Operation not permitted
chown: /var/lib/zabbix/db_data: Operation not permitted
chown: /var/lib/zabbix/snmptraps: Operation not permitted
...
\`\`\`

## Fix

Drop `chown` and `chmod` from the init command and run init-data as the non-root pod user (1997:1995). With `fsGroup: 1995` on the pod's securityContext, kubelet sets group ownership and g+rwX on the emptyDir mount before any container runs, so the init container can `mkdir` the sqlite subdirs as the pod user and the proxy container (also 1997:1995) can write to them.

Applied to both Deployments.

## Test plan

- [ ] ArgoCD syncs new manifest within ~1 min of merge
- [ ] Both Deployments roll new pods, init-data exits 0
- [ ] zabbix-proxy starts, registers with server, joins K3S-ProxyGroup
- [ ] `kubectl get pods -n monitoring -l app=zproxy-k3s` shows `2/2 Running`
- [ ] Zabbix `zabbix.proxy.group.state[K3S-ProxyGroup]` returns to 3 (online)
- [ ] `zabbix.proxy.group.avail.proxies.percent[K3S-ProxyGroup]` returns to 100

title: fix(apt-cache): route deb.debian.org to CDN, not GDA mirror
body:
## Problem

`apt-get update` w kontenerach Debian Bookworm (w tym `docker run`/`docker build` wewnątrz DinD) kończyło się:
```
E: The repository 'http://deb.debian.org/debian-security bookworm-security Release' does not have a Release file.
```

## Root cause

nginx upstream map kierował `deb.debian.org` → `ftp.task.gda.pl`. Mirror GDA hostuje `/debian/` ale **nie `/debian-security/`**. Sprawdzono wszystkich 5 polskich mirrorów z oficjalnej listy Debian — żaden nie replikuje archiwum security.

Debian Bookworm używa `deb.debian.org/debian-security` (nie starego `security.debian.org`), więc oba wpisy w mapie kierowały security traffic na zły upstream → 404 → apt fail.

## Fix

Zmiana upstream dla `deb.debian.org` i `security.debian.org` → `deb.debian.org` CDN (Fastly):
- hostuje zarówno `/debian/` jak i `/debian-security/` ✓
- HTTP 200 bez redirecta do HTTPS ✓
- nginx używa resolveraresolvera `1.1.1.1` (omija CoreDNS rewrite, brak pętli) ✓
- Ubuntu mirrors (`ubuntu.task.gda.pl`) bez zmian ✓

## Co NIE wymaga zmian

- CoreDNS rewrite rules w watchdog — zostają (`deb.debian.org` → apt-cache)
- `/etc/hosts` w DinD sidecar — zostaje
- Cache keys — zostają (`$scheme://$host$request_uri`)

title: fix(arc): mount dind-externals into dind container so container jobs get node
body:
## Problem

Container-based GitHub Actions jobs routed onto the ARC org runners (`builder-org` / scale set `k3s-arc-org`) fail at the very first JS action (`actions/checkout`) with:

```
OCI runtime exec failed: exec failed: unable to start container process:
exec: "/__e/node24/bin/node": stat /__e/node24/bin/node: no such file or directory
```

Surfaced by [Majowka/mesh-manager#473](https://github.com/Majowka/mesh-manager/pull/473), which is the **first** PR to route container-based CI jobs (`Detect Changes`, `Quality Gates`) onto `k3s-arc-org`. The gate/triage jobs previously on this scale set don't use `container:`, so they ran node directly in the `runner` container and never exercised the dind `/__e` path.

## Root cause

In ARC-dind, a `container:` job's node runtime is not in the job image — the dind daemon bind-mounts the runner externals into the job container at `/__e` (`-v /home/runner/externals:/__e`). For that to resolve, the **`dind` container** must have the externals at `/home/runner/externals`.

The `dind` sidecar in both scale sets mounted `dind-sock`, `work`, `docker-config`, `zone-info` — but **not** `dind-externals`. The init container copies node20/node24 into the `dind-externals` emptyDir and the `runner` container mounts it, but the `dind` daemon did not → it bind-mounts an **empty** dir at `/__e` → `/__e/node24/bin/node` missing.

GitHub now defaults node20 actions to node24 server-side (Sep 2025 deprecation), so the missing `node24` is what surfaces.

## Diagnosis (verified on the live cluster)

- Runner image **already ships node24** — not a stale-image problem:
  ```
  kubectl exec -c runner ... -- ls /home/runner/externals
  node20  node20_alpine  node24  node24_alpine
  ```
- The **`dind` container lacked** `/home/runner/externals` (`find node24` in dind → nothing; no `dind-externals` mount).

So it's the dind plumbing, not the runner version.

## Fix

Add the `dind-externals → /home/runner/externals` volumeMount to the `dind` container in both `apps/arc-runner-set/values.yaml` and `apps/arc-runner-set-org/values.yaml` (identical latent bug in both; the volume already exists in `volumes:`).

## Validation

- `yaml.safe_load` parses both files; asserted the mount **and** the referenced volume are present.
- After ArgoCD sync, new ephemeral runner pods will mount externals into dind; re-running mesh-manager#473 should make `Detect Changes` / `Quality Gates` pass.

title: fix(arc): add docker.io + gcr.io mirrors to buildkitd.toml
body:
## Problem

Container **build** jobs (docker/build-push-action in dind) fail to pull their base image:

```
ERROR: failed to solve: failed to resolve source metadata for docker.io/library/python:3.13-slim:
failed to do request: Head "https://registry-1.docker.io/v2/library/python/manifests/3.13-slim":
dial tcp 10.43.x.x:443: i/o timeout
```

Reproduced across zones (different cache ClusterIP each run) on [Majowka/mesh-manager#473](https://github.com/Majowka/mesh-manager/pull/473) — not transient.

## Root cause

`buildkitd.toml` (written by the `configure-registry-mirrors` init container) declared a mirror **only for `mcr.microsoft.com`**. So a build with `FROM python:3.13-slim` (docker.io) had no buildkit mirror and fell back to `registry-1.docker.io`. The `dind` container's `/etc/hosts` override remaps `registry-1.docker.io` → docker-cache ClusterIP, but buildkit then connects on **:443** while the cache only listens on **:5000** → i/o timeout.

`daemon.json` already routes docker.io through `registry-mirrors` (:5000), which is why **job-container** pulls (done by `dockerd`) succeed while **buildkit** builds fail — buildkit uses its own config, not daemon.json.

## Fix

Add explicit `docker.io` and `gcr.io`/`mirror.gcr.io` mirror entries to `buildkitd.toml` (each cache host marked `http`+`insecure`), alongside the existing `mcr.microsoft.com` block. Applied to both `arc-runner-set` and `arc-runner-set-org` (identical init).

## Validation

- `yaml.safe_load` parses both files (utf-8).
- Extracted the embedded TOML and asserted: no duplicate `[registry."…"]` tables, and `docker.io` / `gcr.io` / `mcr.microsoft.com` all present.
- After ArgoCD sync + new runner pods, re-running mesh-manager#473's `Build Containers` should resolve `python:3.13-slim` via the `:5000` mirror.

Follow-up to gitops#88 (dind externals) — both are infra gaps exposed once container jobs actually run on the org ARC runners.

title: fix(registry-cache-gcr): add orphan-cleaner sidecar (short read fix)
body:
## Problem

Distribution registry (`registry:3`) w trybie pull-through zostawia **orphan link files** gdy transient błąd przerwie fetch danych bloba z upstream. Efekt:

1. Manifest cached → link files tworzone dla wszystkich warstw
2. Fetch danych konkretnego bloba failuje (transient 403/timeout od mirror.gcr.io)
3. **Link file zostaje**, data file nie istnieje
4. Kolejne żądania tego bloba: cache widzi link → odpowiada `HTTP 200 + Content-Length: N` → czyta lokalnie → 0 bajtów → Docker: `short read: expected N bytes but got 0`
5. Cache nigdy sam nie wychodzi z tego stanu (link = "mam")

Objaw w CI (`mesh-manager`): `short read: expected 32 bytes but got 0` przy `docker pull mirror.gcr.io/library/redis:7-alpine`.

Root cause potwierdzone na produkcji — VRTX/LDC/AZPL miały identyczny orphan link:
```
library/redis/_layers/sha256/4f4fb700ef54461cfa02571ae0db9a0dc1e0cdb5577484a6d75e68dc38e8acc1/link
```
Przy braku pliku danych. mirror.gcr.io serwuje ten blob poprawnie (HTTP 200, 32B).

Orphan link usunięty ręcznie na wszystkich 3 DC jako hotfix.

## Fix

Sidecar container `orphan-cleaner` (busybox) w każdym z 3 Deploymentów (`vrtx`/`ldc`/`azpl`). Dzieli `emptyDir` z rejestrem, co godzinę skanuje i usuwa link files bez odpowiadających data files, logując co usunął:

```
2026-06-21T21:05:00Z orphan-cleaner: removed library/redis@4f4fb700...
```

title: fix(registry-cache): remove REGISTRY_PROXY_TTL — eliminates orphaned blob corruption
body:
## Problem

CI outage 2026-06-21 16:59 UTC — wszystkie backend joby w mesh-manager (i prawdopodobnie innych repozytoriach) padły z:

\\\
short read: expected 32 bytes but got 0: unexpected EOF
##[error]Docker pull failed with exit code 1
\\\

## Root cause

\sha256:4f4fb700ef54...\ to **32-bajtowy empty gzip layer** obecny w praktycznie każdym Alpine-based image. Błąd w logu dosłownie podaje jego rozmiar: _expected **32 bytes**_.

Sekwencja zdarzeń z TTL=24h:

\\\
T+0h    jakakolwiek Alpine image pullowana → sha256:4f4fb700 zkeszowany, TTL=24h startuje
T+Nh    redis:7-alpine pullowany → cache hit na sha256:4f4fb700, TTL NIE jest resetowany
T+24h   TTL scheduler usuwa dane bloba, link w manifeście zostaje → ORPHAN
T+24h+  docker pull redis:7-alpine → HTTP 200, written=0 → short read: expected 32 bytes
\\\

Shared empty layer ma TTL liczony od najwcześniejszego obrazu który go pobrał — zawsze więc wypada przed resztą warstw konkretnego obrazu. Im popularniejszy blob (ten jest w każdym Alpine image), tym wcześniej TTL ekspiruje.

**Doraźny fix:** ręczne usunięcie bloba z obu cache (VRTX + LDC) + \egistry garbage-collect\ — wykonane 2026-06-21.

## Fix

Usunięcie \REGISTRY_PROXY_TTL\ ze wszystkich 9 Deploymentów. Bez TTL scheduler nie startuje → żadne blobs nie są eviktowane przez czas → zero orphanów.

**Zarządzanie rozmiarem cache** bez TTL:
- \emptyDir sizeLimit: 10Gi\ → kubelet eviction gdy pod przekroczy limit (czysty restart, zimny cache)
- Obecne zużycie: ~1.1G per instancja → 9x headroom

## Zmienione pliki (9)

| App | Plik |
|-----|------|
| registry-cache | \egistry-cache.yaml\, \zone-ldc.yaml\, \zone-azpl.yaml\ |
| registry-cache-gcr | \egistry-cache-gcr.yaml\, \zone-ldc.yaml\, \zone-azpl.yaml\ |
| registry-cache-mcr | \egistry-cache-mcr.yaml\, \zone-ldc.yaml\, \zone-azpl.yaml\ |

Każdy plik: -2 linie (\REGISTRY_PROXY_TTL\ name + value). Zero innych zmian.

## Summary
- `k3s-arc-org` is currently capped at `maxRunners: 6` (set in #122, when only 4 worker nodes — k3s-worker4-7 — existed). Since then 3 more nodes joined the pool (`sysclay-k3s-worker-1/2/3`, 2026-09-06), so real node capacity for runners grew from 4 to 7.
- Listener logs show the scale set pinned at max=6 for ~63% of recent samples, with GitHub's `assigned job` count exceeding 6 (hit 7) twice — real job queueing at the ceiling, not just idle capacity.
- `k3s-arc-org-fast` (max=10) stays comfortably underutilized (assigned job 2-3) — this is specifically an `org` (non-fast) capacity gap.

## Why 7 is safe (same logic as #122, updated node count)
- 7 schedulable nodes now available for runners: `k3s-worker4-7` (LDC, 8 vCPU/8Gi each) + `sysclay-k3s-worker-1/2/3` (4 vCPU/16Gi each).
- The scale set's soft `topologySpreadConstraints` (`hostname` maxSkew=1) keeps 1 runner+dind pod pair per physical node while node count ≥ runner count — at max=7 this still holds, no node gets doubled up.
- Runner+dind pods have no memory `limits`, only `requests` (2.5Gi + 1.5Gi = 4Gi/pod). Doubling up on an 8Gi LDC worker would consume the node's entire allocatable memory from requests alone — real OOM risk that only appears once max exceeds schedulable node count (currently 7). Sysclay nodes (16Gi) would tolerate 2 pods memory-wise but are already CPU-tight (75-87% requested).

## Test plan
- [ ] ArgoCD syncs `apps/arc-runner-set-org` and reconciles `AutoscalingRunnerSet/k3s-arc-org` to `maxRunners: 7`
- [ ] `kubectl get autoscalingrunnersets -n arc-runners k3s-arc-org` shows `MAX 7`
- [ ] Watch listener logs for `assigned job` no longer pinned above `decision` during a busy period
- [ ] Confirm no more than 1 runner pod per node (`kubectl get pods -n arc-runners -o wide`)

title: perf(arc-runner-set-org): right-size runner/dind requests, minRunners 2 -> 1
body:
## Summary

Right-sizes the `builder-org` ARC scale set (`k3s-arc-org`, `apps/arc-runner-set-org`) used by Majowka/mesh-manager CI, based on 10 live-profiled CI runs (2026-09-24). Epic: Majowka/mesh-manager#5295. Related: Majowka/mesh-manager#5485 (dind CPU request), Majowka/mesh-manager#5486 (memory requests). Evidence: [`docs/ci/arc-resource-profiling.md`](https://github.com/Majowka/mesh-manager/blob/develop/docs/ci/arc-resource-profiling.md).

Maintainer-approved scope: CPU split, memory, minRunners. `maxRunners` (#5484), images, init containers, `arc-runner-set` and `arc-runner-set-org-fast` are **not** touched. Values-only change: the chart stays pinned at `gha-runner-scale-set` 0.14.2, so no chart/version bump is needed.

## ⚠️ Sync policy: merging deploys

`apps/arc-runner-set-org/Application.yaml` has `syncPolicy.automated: { prune: true, selfHeal: true }`, and the values source tracks `targetRevision: main`. **Merging this PR rolls it out to the cluster automatically within about 3 minutes.** Running runner pods keep their old spec. New pods (and the ephemeral runners ARC recreates after each job) get the new one. This PR is a draft on purpose; merge it at a quiet moment when someone can watch.

## Before / after

| Setting | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `runner` CPU request | 2000m | **500m** |
| `runner` memory request = limit | 2500Mi | **1024Mi** |
| `dind` CPU request | 1000m | **2000m** |
| `dind` memory request = limit | 1500Mi | 1500Mi (unchanged, see below) |
| CPU limits | none | none (unchanged, bursting intended) |
| **Pod total** | **3 CPU / 4000Mi** | **2.5 CPU / 2524Mi** |
| `minRunners` | 2 | **1** |
| `maxRunners` | 15 | 15 (unchanged) |

## Evidence per value

- **runner CPU 500m**: observed 64-1300m across every profiled job class. It never came close to the 2000m request. There's no limit, so it can still burst to 1.3 CPU when the node has spare capacity.
- **dind CPU 2000m** (raised from 1500m in review): observed medians were 1150-2170m on Docker-heavy classes (`test-suite`, `bridge-stack smoke`, backend unit and real-integration shards), with a max around 2700m. dind was already running at 1.15-2.7x its 1000m request, and that usage was invisible to the scheduler. The request now covers the typical Docker-heavy median, so CFS CPU shares under node contention match real use and a busy dind isn't squeezed to a smaller share than it needs. There is still no CPU limit, so bursting to the ~2700m peaks remains allowed.
- **runner memory 1024Mi**: the observed max was 320Mi in the profiling campaign and about 520Mi in the 5-day sample quoted in #123, so there is at least 2x headroom.
- **dind memory stays 1500Mi**: the target was 1024Mi, but I kept the current value. Reasons:
  - The worker nodes run Ubuntu 24.04 with containerd 2.x, which means cgroup v2 with a private cgroup namespace. dockerd therefore creates the nested job, service and build containers **under the dind container's cgroup**. The pod-level dind number (512Mi max, `bridge-stack smoke`) already includes those containers, and so does the memory limit. An OOM here kills the whole Docker stack of the job.
  - The profiling doc does not give a per-class dind max for the `real-integration` shards, which are the heaviest memory users: the job container running pytest plus `celery --concurrency=2`, TimescaleDB, Redis and Mosquitto. It only gives the 25-512Mi range across all classes. Sampling was every 20s via metrics-server working set, and per-container stats inside DinD were not collectible.
  - TimescaleDB's shared buffers fill lazily over a long test run. `test-frontend` runs node with `--max-old-space-size=3072` inside dind. The campaign covered only `ci.yml` runs.
  - 1024Mi would be exactly 2x the one reported max, not at least 2x the verified real-integration peak. Lowering dind memory is left for a follow-up once per-class dind maxima for real-integration are measured.
- **minRunners 1**: the idle warm pool now holds 2.5 CPU instead of 6. Only the first job after an idle period lands on the warm runner. Any concurrent or later job still waits for a new pod to start (scheduling, image pull, registration), the same as today once the warm pool is used up.

Live snapshot while preparing this PR (read-only `kubectl`): a `k3s-arc-org` pod was Pending with `0/13 nodes are available: 3 Insufficient cpu, ... 4 Insufficient memory`. Memory is also blocking placement on the 8Gi LDC workers, so the 4000Mi → 2524Mi reduction matters as well as the CPU change.

## Expected effect

- About 44 allocatable CPU on the Ready workers. Before, that fit about 14 builder-org pods at 3 CPU (`maxRunners: 15` × 3 = 45 CPU, more than the whole fleet). After, it fits about 17 pods at 2.5 CPU. That's **roughly 20% more concurrent builder-org pods** on the same hardware, and `maxRunners: 15` × 2.5 = 37.5 CPU now fits under the fleet total. The fleet is shared with non-CI workloads, so real headroom is somewhat lower.
- Fewer `FailedScheduling Insufficient cpu/memory` waits. These were the dominant attributable queue cause in the profiling doc (14% of queued observations), with real-integration shards queuing 15-27 min at the median.
- About 1.5 GiB less memory reserved per pod, so more builder-org pods fit on the 8Gi LDC workers.
- Idle reservation drops from 6 CPU / 8000Mi to 2.5 CPU / 2524Mi.

## Canary / verification plan (after sync)

1. `kubectl get autoscalingrunnerset -n arc-runners k3s-arc-org`: MINIMUM RUNNERS should show 1. Then `kubectl get pods -n arc-runners -l app.kubernetes.io/part-of=gha-runner-scale-set -o wide`, and on a new `k3s-arc-org-*` pod confirm the new requests: `kubectl get pod <pod> -n arc-runners -o jsonpath='{.spec.initContainers[?(@.name=="dind")].resources}{"\n"}{.spec.containers[?(@.name=="runner")].resources}'`.
2. For the next 5-10 mesh-manager CI runs, watch for OOMs and restarts: `kubectl get pods -n arc-runners -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,RESTARTS:.status.containerStatuses[*].restartCount,LAST:.status.containerStatuses[*].lastState.terminated.reason`, plus `kubectl get events -n arc-runners --field-selector reason=OOMKilling` and `kubectl describe` of any failed runner pod. Watch the `runner` container in particular on jobs that run tools directly in it rather than in a `container:`: `bridge-go.yml` golangci-lint, `go test -race`, cross-compiles, and `regression-evidence.yml`. None of these were in the profiling campaign.
3. Scheduling: `kubectl get events -n arc-runners --field-selector reason=FailedScheduling`. Expect fewer `Insufficient cpu` / `Insufficient memory` events than before.
4. Queue delays: attach mesh-manager's `scripts/ci/profile-arc-run.py` (read-only) to the next 5-10 `🏗️ CI Pipeline` runs and compare the `k8s_unschedulable_cpu` share and the queue delays for real-integration shards and `bridge-stack smoke` against the baseline tables in the profiling doc. Also check that dind CPU contention hasn't made runtimes noticeably slower.
5. `kubectl top pod -n arc-runners --containers` during real-integration shards, to fill the per-class dind memory gap before any later dind memory reduction.

Abort criteria: any `OOMKilled` runner or dind container, or "runner lost communication" failures that correlate with the rollout. If either happens, roll back.

## Rollback

Revert this PR's squash-merge commit (`git revert <sha>` → PR → merge). ArgoCD syncs the previous values automatically, and new runner pods pick up the old shape. No state or data migration is involved.

title: fix(metrics-server): take over from k3s addon, pin to control-plane

## Problem
`kubectl top nodes` zwraca `<unknown>` dla 12 z 13 węzłów, a `metrics.k8s.io` zwraca puste listy lub NotFound.

- Addon k3s `metrics-server` nie ma `nodeSelector`. Ręczny pin do control-plane istniał tylko na starym `k3s-master` (VRTX). k3s i tak nadpisuje packaged manifesty przy starcie serwera.

- Ścieżka master→kubelet działa (sprawdzone przez `kubectl logs` na worker5, sysclay-2 i sysclay-3).

## Zmiana
- Nowa aplikacja `apps/metrics-server`: chart `metrics-server` 3.13.1 (app 0.8.1, ta sama wersja co obecny addon).
- `nodeSelector: node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: "true"` plus tolerations `CriticalAddonsOnly` i `control-plane:NoSchedule`.
- Argumenty takie same jak w addonie k3s.
- README: metrics-server przeniesiony do GitOps.

## Kolejność wdrożenia (ważne)
1. Na **wszystkich** masterach (k3s-master2, 3, 4): dodać `disable: [metrics-server]` do `/etc/rancher/k3s/config.yaml` i restartować k3s **po jednym węźle**. k3s usunie wtedy zasoby addonu.
2. Dopiero potem merge. Bez kroku 1 sync się wywali: selector Deploymentu jest inny i niemutowalny (sprawdzone w `kubectl apply --dry-run=server`).

## Test
- `helm template` z tymi values, potem `kubectl apply --dry-run=server`. Jedyny błąd to oczekiwany immutable selector na istniejącym Deploymencie addonu.

title: feat(arc): AKS burst AutoscalingRunnerSet — elastic overflow for k3s-arc-org
body:
## What

Adds a **second** `AutoscalingRunnerSet` (ARC) targeting a new AKS cluster (`aks-azpl-burst`, Azure Poland Central, Spot `Standard_D8as_v5` node pool, autoscaling 0→8) as elastic burst capacity for `k3s-arc-org` — the on-prem scale set that runs GitHub Actions org-level jobs under `runs-on: [self-hosted, builder-org]`.

- `apps/arc-runner-set-org-aks-burst/` — the new `AutoscalingRunnerSet` (Application + values). Template copied verbatim from `apps/arc-runner-set-org/values.yaml` (same image, same runner+dind resource split: ~2.5 vCPU / ~2.5Gi per pod), with these deltas only:
  - **GitHub identity**: same `githubConfigUrl` (`https://github.com/majowka`), same implicit "Default" runner group (no `runnerGroup` set, matching `arc-runner-set-org`), same `scaleSetLabels` (`self-hosted`, `builder-org`) — so GitHub pools jobs across both clusters' listeners for the same `runs-on`, with zero extra GitHub-side config.
  - **`runnerScaleSetName` differs** (`aks-burst-arc-org` vs `k3s-arc-org`): GitHub requires scale-set names to be unique *within* a runner group ("Runner scale set names are unique within the runner group they belong to" — GitHub docs, also documented in `Majowka/infrastructure`'s `docs/plans/arc-multi-cluster-ha.md`). Since both clusters deliberately stay in the same (Default) group here, the name has to differ instead — pooling still works because GitHub matches on labels/group, not scale-set name.
  - **Registry-cache/zone logic dropped**: the on-prem `configure-registry-mirrors` init container points `dockerd`/`buildkitd` at in-cluster `registry-cache-${ZONE}.arc-runners.svc.cluster.local` Services — unreachable from a separate AKS cluster (different cluster-DNS, no Tailscale/VPN link by design). Dropped entirely; `dind` falls back to stock defaults (direct pulls from public registries). `topologySpreadConstraints`' zone-based skew (tied to our 3 on-prem DCs) is dropped for the same reason; the hostname-based one is kept.
  - **Spot toleration** added (`kubernetes.azure.com/scalesetpriority=spot:NoSchedule`) so pods can schedule onto AKS's auto-tainted Spot pool.
  - **`minRunners: 0` / `maxRunners: 24`**: burst capacity should scale to zero, not sit warm; 24 ≈ 8 nodes × ~3 runner pods/node at this resource sizing, matching the tf-azure node pool.
- `apps/arc-aks-burst/` — the ARC controller (`gha-runner-scale-set-controller`) for the new cluster. **Not explicitly requested in scope but required**: an `AutoscalingRunnerSet` needs a controller running on the *same* cluster (confirmed in `docs/plans/arc-multi-cluster-ha.md`, "nie jest opcjonalne"). Mirrors `apps/arc/Application.yaml` 1:1 besides `destination`/`metadata.name`.

## Explicit dependencies before this reconciles (do not merge-and-forget)

1. **tf-azure PR** provisioning `aks-azpl-burst` must be applied first.
2. **`destination` is a placeholder** (`name: aks-azpl-burst`) in both `Application.yaml` files — the cluster isn't registered with this ArgoCD instance yet. After the tf-azure PR applies, someone runs `argocd cluster add` with the new AKS kubeconfig (manual/semi-manual, out of band — not something a GitOps PR can do). Until then both Applications will fail to reconcile (unknown destination), by design — that's the intended signal that step 2 hasn't happened yet.
3. **`arc-github-secret-org`** (the `githubConfigSecret`) must exist in the `arc-runners` namespace on the new cluster before the runner set can register with GitHub. This repo has no existing ExternalSecret/Infisical manifest for this secret on the *existing* cluster either (it's provisioned out of band today), so the same out-of-band step needs to be repeated for the new cluster — not something this PR can do blind, and nothing here hardcodes or duplicates the credential.

## Registry-mirror behavior difference vs on-prem

On-prem `k3s-arc-org` accelerates image pulls through an in-cluster registry-cache topology (per-zone Services + a `zone-labeler` DaemonSet). None of that exists on AKS and it can't reach the on-prem Services (different cluster, no cross-cluster networking by design). This variant's `dind` runs with stock Docker defaults — direct pulls from the real registries, no `registry-mirrors`/`insecure-registries` entries. Net effect: no caching benefit, slightly slower first pulls, but no functional breakage — `docker.io`/GCR/MCR pulls all still work, just uncached.

title: fix(arc): ServerSideApply=true for arc-aks-burst controller CRDs
body:
## Summary
Live symptom on `aks-azpl-burst` after cluster registration: `arc-aks-burst-gha-rs-controller` pod stuck in `CrashLoopBackOff` (`unable to setup indexers: no matches for kind "EphemeralRunnerSet"`), and the ArgoCD Application `SyncFailed` on all 4 ARC CRDs:

```
metadata.annotations: Too long: may not be more than 262144 bytes
```

Client-side `kubectl apply` stores the full previous manifest in the `kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration` annotation, which can't hold ARC's large CRD OpenAPI schemas. Fix: `ServerSideApply=true` in `syncOptions`.

`apps/arc/Application.yaml` (on-prem) already has this exact setting for the same reason — this file's own header comment claimed to mirror it 1:1 but this option was missed. Confirmed fix pattern against the working on-prem config, not guessed.

title: fix(arc): correct controllerServiceAccount name for aks-burst-arc-org
body:
## Summary
Live symptom on `aks-azpl-burst` after the controller came up (post gitops#132): `AutoscalingRunnerSet` reconcile loop stuck on:
```
failed to resolve app config: failed to get kubernetes secret: "arc-runners/arc-github-secret-org"
```
Misleading — the Secret was present the whole time (copied over manually earlier). Root cause: `controllerServiceAccount.name` in `values.yaml` was copied verbatim from on-prem, where the controller's Helm release is literally named `arc` → SA `arc-gha-rs-controller`. This cluster's controller release is `arc-aks-burst` (per `apps/arc-aks-burst/Application.yaml`) → actual SA is `arc-aks-burst-gha-rs-controller`, confirmed live via `kubectl get sa -n arc-systems` on `aks-azpl-burst`. Azure LowPriorityCores quota is stuck at 20 vCPU on this subscription (self-service increase broken — see internal memory). 20/8vCPU per D8as_v5 = 2 nodes max = ~6 runners real ceiling right now.

title: fix(zproxy-k3s): pre-create ssl dirs in init-data, pin image digest
body:
## Problem

zproxy-k3s-1 stuck in CrashLoopBackOff (469+ restarts, 39h) — details in #140.

### Root cause (fundamentalny)

Cały /var/lib/zabbix był montowany jako jeden ^[mptyDir. To shaduje **wszystkie** podkatalogi które obraz ma wbudowane (z build-time). init-data init container próbował je odtworzyć przez mkdir -p, ale to był plaster na złą architekturę — każda zmiana upstream entrypointu mogła dodać nowy katalog i wywołać kolejny crashloop.

Upstream commit zabbix/zabbix-docker@5042789a (2026-09-15) wprowadził openssl_prepare_ca() — robi cp -a ssl/ssl_ca/. ssl/ssl_ca_internal/ bez sprawdzania istnienia katalogów. ssl/ssl_ca był zgubiony przez blob ^[mptyDir → crashloop.

## Zmiany w tym PR

### 1. Refaktor architektury woluminów (właściwy fix)

Zamiast jednego ^[mptyDir na /var/lib/zabbix, montujemy **tylko 3 konkretne podkatalogi** które muszą być zapisywalne:

| Volume | Typ | Mount |
|--------|-----|-------|
| db-data | ^[mptyDir 256Mi | /var/lib/zabbix/db_data |
| snmptraps | ^[mptyDir 64Mi | /var/lib/zabbix/snmptraps |
| ssl-ca-internal | ^[mptyDir{medium:Memory} 32Mi | /var/lib/zabbix/ssl/ssl_ca_internal |

Wszystkie inne ścieżki (ssl/certs, ssl/keys, ssl/ssl_ca, ^[nc, ssh_keys, mibs…) pozostają nienaruszone z warstwy obrazu — zgodnie z upstream compose_zabbix_components.yaml.

ssl_ca_internal używa medium:Memory (k8s odpowiednik 	mpfs) bo openssl_prepare_ca() robi m -rf + cp -a przy każdym starcie — musi być zapisywalny i jest z natury efemeryczny.

### 2. Usunięcie init-data init container

Nie jest już potrzebny —  sGroup:1995 nadal działa i kubelet chownuje indywidualne emptyDir-y do gid 1995 z g+rwX przed uruchomieniem kontenera.

### 3. Pin obrazu do digest

Obraz przypięty do sha256:af920211... (post-09-15 build) — oba replikaty biegną ten sam, przetestowany build. Floating tag nie może już cicho rozjechać worker5 vs worker6.

### 4. ZBX_DEBUGLEVEL 3→2

Extended debug nie jest odpowiedni dla produkcji.

## Zabbix alert

Proxy group [K3S-ProxyGroup]: Availability too low — wyczyści się po restarcie zproxy-k3s-1 z nowym manifestem przez ArgoCD.

Closes #140
